source.summary: The draft is the official section maincard for printed section 58, not an invented n58 topic. Its English title and chapter match the official TOC. All 10 source objects, source_refs, source_text, printed pages, the footnote, and embedded raw source are retained. Modern scientific qualifications match the current Chinese lesson; its existence and ready status are not evidence of historical science approval.

historicalIdentity.assessment: Same historical physicist and contributions. The source initials, British identity, and 1831-1879 life dates are retained literally; no identity substitution is needed.

Same source radio researcher, with source initials retained literally. Describing him as an important early participant rather than the sole inventor preserves the person while qualifying the source's exclusive invention attribution. This is not an endorsement of the source initials as a normalized English biographical spelling.
The analogy to Newton's laws remains an analogy between foundations of classical theories, not an invented contribution.

numbersMathAndConditions.historicalPeriod: second half of the nineteenth century
numbersMathAndConditions.assessment: No numerical value, unit, mathematical relation, or task has been altered or invented. Maxwell's equations are named, not displayed. Source absolutes about forces, gravity, life, and invention priority are qualified consistently with the Chinese comparison text.

science.summary: No substantive physical or historical misattribution was found in the frozen English claims. Passing scientific meaning does not make the definitions sufficiently accessible to the target reader.

checks.assessment: Macroscopic mechanics and molecular thermal motion are distinguished without claiming that these subjects never investigate interactions. Classical electrodynamics includes charges, currents, fields, interactions, and field propagation. Fields carrying energy and momentum and mediating charged-body interactions is appropriate at this introductory level.

The four interactions are correctly listed. Elasticity, friction, and muscle forces mainly involve electromagnetic microscopic mechanisms, with quantum, material, and biochemical qualifications. The weak-interaction footnote correctly limits the claim to certain transformations and decays.

Light is an electromagnetic wave. Orbital weightlessness is explained by approximate free fall and small support forces, not disappearing gravity. Long-term bodily effects are not denied. Removing electromagnetism is explicitly hypothetical, not a feasible switch-off experiment.

Nuclear binding is primarily attributed to the strong interaction between nucleons, with proton electromagnetic repulsion retained. Atomic and molecular structure require electromagnetic interactions and quantum laws. Gravity is not confined to large scales; electrical neutrality qualifies astronomical dominance. The short-range statement is appropriate to the elementary nuclear-force context, and macroscopic weak-decay effects are not excluded.

Maxwell's field theory, classical equations, kinetic-theory contribution, and use of probability/statistical methods are correctly attributed. The draft avoids an unsupported claim that he was the first to use statistics anywhere in physics.

Rubbed amber is an electrostatic observation, not a radio experiment. Maxwell's inclusion of magnetic effects of changing electric fields and prediction of waves are theoretical contributions; he is not credited with the later experimental demonstration or sole invention of radio. Popov's early practical role is retained without sole-inventor priority. Early motors are correctly allowed to precede Maxwell's complete field theory while using experimentally established electromagnetic laws. Theory, experiment, and engineering are not forced into one universal chronological order.
Electrical energy and communication applications remain foundations of modern society, followed by the source's invitation to study basic electromagnetic laws.

sequence.assessment: The introductory overview is consistent with electrostatics, current, magnetism, unified fields, and electromagnetic waves. The official 9p TOC places electrostatics before steady current/current in media, then the magnetic field of current and induction. Electric fields already occur within electrostatics, so this is not a claim that all fields come after magnetism. Mentioning waves here does not invent a new N58 topic or a new 9p waves chapter.

readability.reader: A strong eight-year-old independently reading a serious introductory physics lesson.
readability.summary: The draft provides useful explanations for macroscopic, interaction, thermal motion, free fall, electrical neutrality, probability, and statistical methods. However, the central charge/field/wave explanation still depends on undefined abstractions, the nucleus passage substitutes unfamiliar particle names for an explanation, and the history passage compresses its causal sequence into adult academic phrasing. These are local comprehension repairs, not a request to simplify away the physics.

flow.summary: All 24 saved paragraphs exactly match the draft's nine prose blocks in order. All six saved break anchors match the draft. The sequence moves from the subject definition to everyday interactions, light/free fall, interactions at different scales, Maxwell, historical development, applications, and the learning objective. The portrait remains between paragraphs 16 and 17; the footnote remains after its interaction discussion. Readability repairs must update their saved paragraphs and affected break-anchor strings together.

findings.title: Give charge, field, and wave a non-circular physical meaning
quotes: Electric charge is the property through which objects participate in electromagnetic interactions
An electromagnetic field describes electric and magnetic effects throughout space.
An electromagnetic wave is a disturbance of an electromagnetic field that travels through space.
findings.finding: Charge is explained through the very electromagnetic interaction being introduced, while electric and magnetic effects remain unnamed effects. Disturbance and propagation introduce more abstractions rather than explaining what travels. A strong young reader can repeat these sentences without learning what charged objects do or what changes in a wave. The later definition of interaction does not supply the missing physical meaning.

smallestRepair.scope: Replace only the short definitions in paragraph 2 and the wave-definition sentence in paragraph 8; keep the bold scope statement, source refs, and adjacent scientific qualifications.
smallestRepair.paragraph2: Change propagation in the bold sentence to travel. Suggested replacement for the following definitions: Electric charge is a property of matter. Charges can be positive or negative, and charged objects can push one another apart or pull one another closer. Electric current is a flow of charge with an overall direction. An electromagnetic field has electric and magnetic parts spread through space. Its electric part can push or pull a charged particle. Its magnetic part can change the motion of a moving charged particle.
smallestRepair.paragraph8Sentence2: An electromagnetic wave is a change in the electric and magnetic parts of a field that travels through space.
smallestRepair.preserve: Do not reduce the field to a picture, a material fluid, or a force acting only through contact; retain the following statement that fields carry energy and momentum.

findings.title: Explain the nuclear terms and name the quantum-law referent
quotes: In an atomic nucleus, the strong interaction between nucleons, the protons and neutrons in the nucleus, plays the main role in binding them together.
They must also obey quantum laws.
findings.finding: Nucleons receives a list of two new particle names, but neither the nucleus nor the charges of those particles is explained. The reader consequently lacks the reason for proton repulsion in the next sentence. They then has a broad antecedent list of arrangements, bonds, and properties; naming the structures and properties would make the qualification unambiguous.

smallestRepair.scope: Add a brief nucleus/particle gloss at paragraph 13 and replace the final pronoun sentence in paragraph 14. No additional atomic-physics lesson is needed.
smallestRepair.paragraph13: The nucleus is the small central part of an atom. It contains protons and usually neutrons. Protons have positive electric charge, while neutrons have no electric charge. These particles are called nucleons. The strong interaction between nucleons plays the main role in holding the nucleus together. Protons also repel one another through the electromagnetic interaction, which affects the properties of the nucleus.
smallestRepair.paragraph14Sentence2: To explain these structures and properties, we also need quantum laws.
smallestRepair.preserve: Retain both strong-interaction binding and electromagnetic repulsion; do not replace nuclear binding with electric attraction or remove the quantum qualification.

findings.title: Separate the observation, theoretical prediction, and later practical work
quotes: This history extends from observations that amber, a hardened tree resin, attracts small, light objects after being rubbed with silk to British physicist J. C. Maxwell's inclusion of the magnetic effects of changing electric fields in his theory.

The relationship between theory and technology is not a one-way sequence: steam engines came before a mature theory of thermal processes, and early electric motors came before Maxwell's complete electromagnetic field theory.
findings.finding: The from/to sentence embeds the early observation inside an abstract history/inclusion construction. The later one-way sequence sentence combines two comparisons before the reader reaches the experiment-versus-theory explanation. The scientific attribution is sound, but a young independent reader has to reconstruct who observed, who predicted, and what later experiments and builders contributed.

smallestRepair.scope: Split the history construction into direct statements and split the first comparison sentence of paragraph 21. Keep paragraph 20's literal A. C. Popov and multiple-researcher qualification.
smallestRepair.paragraph19: Electrodynamics grew through experiments, theoretical research, and work on new devices. One early observation was that amber, a hardened tree resin, attracted small, light objects after being rubbed with silk. Much later, British physicist J. C. Maxwell developed a theory connecting electricity and magnetism. It included the magnetic effects of changing electric fields. From his theory, he predicted that electromagnetic waves could travel through space. Later experiments supported that prediction. His theory provided an important basis for later radio technology.
smallestRepair.paragraph21FirstSentence: Theory and technology did not always develop in the same order. Steam engines came before a fully developed theory of heat. Early electric motors also came before Maxwell's complete electromagnetic field theory.
smallestRepair.preserve: Keep the remaining distinction between experimentally established motor laws and the theory plus later experiments used in radio development. Do not attribute experimental discovery of waves or sole invention of radio to Maxwell, require all motors to postdate him, change source initials, or add a new historical name/date.
